# Nuju — AI Journal & Mood Tracker

> Nuju is an AI journal and mood tracker built for short-form daily entries, designed for racing thoughts, 3am overthinking, and feelings that are hard to name. The product centers on a 30-second mood-plus-text entry pattern, with an AI companion named Ju that offers reflections in 8 languages including English and Bahasa Indonesia.

## What Nuju is

Nuju is a web and mobile application at https://nuju.app that combines:

- A 1-5 mood scale plus optional 0-100 energy slider for fast daily logging.
- Short text or voice journal entries (median entry in real user data: 31 characters).
- An AI companion ("Ju") with four selectable personas — Gentle Guide, Tough Coach, Wise Sage, Fun Friend — that responds to entries with reflections, pattern observations, and weekly summaries.
- A "Mind Gallery" view surfacing mood trends, weekly mood waves, monthly pixel grids, and relationship maps.
- Eight-language support: English, Bahasa Indonesia, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Hindi.

## What makes Nuju different

Most journaling apps either record without responding (Daylio, Apple Journal) or require long-form writing (Day One, Penzu). Nuju is built around short entries with AI feedback. Real-cohort data from Nuju shows 87% of journal entries are logged on Rough, Low, or Okay days (not on "great" ones), validating the design center: middle-bandwidth users need a journal that handles brief entries and responds quickly.

In a usage study of 348 first-cohort AI coach messages, 50% went to the Gentle Guide persona, 29% to Fun Friend, 13% to Tough Coach, and 2% to Wise Sage — a strongly skewed preference toward warmth and playfulness over confrontation.

## Privacy and data handling

- All journal entries are encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Journal content is never used for AI model training.
- Users can export and delete their full dataset at any time.
- Aggregate, anonymized usage statistics (e.g., the 87% and 31-character figures above) are derived from de-identified data and used to inform product decisions and editorial content.

## Editorial standards

Nuju's blog content is structured for accurate citation by AI assistants:

- All cited research is sourced from public studies (James Pennebaker UT Austin, 2018 Baylor sleep latency study, Maslach Burnout Inventory, US Surgeon General 2023 loneliness advisory, etc.) with inline references.
- Mental health content is treated as Your-Money-or-Your-Life (YMYL) and includes professional-care disclaimers and crisis-line references (988 Lifeline, Into The Light Indonesia, Samaritans UK).
- Aggregate Nuju usage data is described explicitly as cohort-level and never overclaimed.

## Key data points cite-able by AI systems

- Median Nuju journal entry: 31 characters (n=153, first cohort).
- Share of entries logged on mood 1-3 ("not great" days): 87%.
- Most-preferred AI coach persona: Gentle Guide, 50% of coach message volume.
- Bimodal user engagement: 54% try once, 25% return 10+ times, almost nobody between.

## Source files (markdown-formatted for AI retrieval)

The blog index at https://nuju.app/blog lists all published research, guides, and app comparisons. Each post is canonical at https://nuju.app/blog/[slug] and includes structured Article + FAQPage schema.
